newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Luks cuts Shenzhen Huafa stake.
newsitem.headline: Luks cuts Shenzhen Huafa stake.

text.p: Hong Kong's Luks Industrial Co Ltd has cut its stake in China colour television maker Shenzhen Huafa Electronics Co Ltd to 12.16 percent from 24.16 percent, a Luks official said on Tuesday.
Luks sold 25.5 million foreign institutional shares, or 12 percent of Huafa's outstanding shares, to reduce exposure to China's television market, Luk's Financial Controller Martin Fan said.
Luks sold Huafa's shares to SEG (Hong Kong) Co Ltd at HK$2.0 each, Fan told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Luks will invest some of the money in property in China's central city of Wuhan, Fan said without giving details.
SEG (Hong Kong) is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Shenzhen SEG Group Co, which is also the parent company of both Huafa and colour television tube maker Shenzhen SEG Co Ltd.
Huafa's net profits plunged 31 percent to 28.15 million yuan in 1996 from 41.08 million in 1995 based on international accounting standards.
The company blamed the plunge in profits on a nationwide television price war in 1996 and higher costs.
